risk-disclosure.title: Virtual Asset Risk Disclosure
risk-disclosure.subtitle: Risk Disclosure Statement — Metacomp FZE, Virtual Asset Broker-Dealer Services. Issued in accordance with Part V (Public Disclosures) of the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook.

blocks.text: Issued in accordance with Rule V.B of the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook.
ARTICLE 1 – MATERIAL RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH VIRTUAL ASSETS

1.1. Clients and prospective clients should read this Statement carefully and should not acquire, hold, deal in, or transact in Virtual Assets unless they understand and are willing to accept the risks involved, including the risk of losing the entire value of their Virtual Assets.
1.2. The Company discloses that all Virtual Assets are subject to material risks. In particular, and without limitation, Virtual Assets:
A. may lose their value in part or in full, and are subject to extreme price volatility at times;
B. may not be liquid, and a client may be unable to buy, sell, or otherwise dispose of a Virtual Asset at the desired time or price, and may face liquidity limitations;
C. may not always be transferable, and some transfers may be irreversible and may not always be possible;
D. may be transacted in ways that are not private, and some transactions are recorded on public Distributed Ledger Technology (“DLT”) and may be visible to, and traceable by, third parties; and
E. may be subject to fraud, manipulation, or theft, including through hacks and other targeted schemes, and may not benefit from legal protections.
ARTICLE 2 – ADDITIONAL RISKS RELEVANT TO THE COMPANY’S SERVICES
2.1. In addition to the risks in Article 1, clients should have regard to the following risks relevant to the Company’s VA Activity, without limitation:

A. principal-dealing and pricing risk – the Company acts as principal counterparty and quotes prices at a spread, and the price a client receives reflects that spread and prevailing market conditions;
B. settlement and transfer risk – virtual-asset settlement occurs on-chain to the client’s nominated wallet, and an incorrect wallet address or a failed or irreversible transfer may result in loss;
C. technology and smart-contract risk – Virtual Assets and their supporting protocols, smart contracts, and infrastructure may contain defects, may fail, or may be subject to cyber-attack;
D. counterparty and liquidity-provider risk – the Company offsets inventory through external liquidity providers, each of which carries operational and counterparty risk; and
E. regulatory risk – the legal and regulatory treatment of Virtual Assets may change, which may adversely affect their value, transferability, or availability.

2.2. For the avoidance of doubt, Client Money held in connection with the Company’s services does not benefit from any form of deposit protection. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results, and any forward-looking statement is subject to the risks and uncertainties described in this Statement.

conflict-of-interest.title: Conflict of Interest
conflict-of-interest.subtitle: Conflict of Interest Disclosure Policy — Metacomp FZE, Virtual Asset Broker-Dealer Services.

blocks.text: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

Metacomp FZE (“Metacomp” or the “Company”) is committed to conducting its Virtual Asset Broker-Dealer activities with integrity, objectivity, and fairness, and to ensuring that the interests of its clients are protected at all times. This Conflict of Interest Disclosure Policy (the “Policy”) sets out the arrangements through which the Company identifies, prevents, manages, discloses, and monitors actual, potential, and perceived conflicts of interest arising in the course of its business.

This Policy is established in accordance with the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook, the VARA Company Rulebook, and the VARA Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook, and is consistent with the Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook and the Technology and Information Rulebook, together with Dubai Law No. (4) of 2022 Regulating Virtual Assets in the Emirate of Dubai, the VARA Virtual Assets and Related Activities Regulations 2023, and applicable UAE federal law. It supplements, and is to be read together with, the Company’s Corporate Governance Policy and Framework, the Broker-Dealer Operational Policy and Procedures, the Compliance Management Framework, the AML/CFT Policy and Procedures, and the Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy.

The Company confirms that it takes all reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest involving the Company, its Group, its Board, its Staff, its clients, and its investors, and that any conflict which cannot reasonably be avoided is appropriately managed, recorded, and disclosed so as to ensure that clients are treated fairly and that the Company’s objectivity and independence in conducting Virtual Asset Activities are not compromised.

This Policy applies to all members of the Board of Directors, Responsible Individuals, Senior Management, control-function holders, employees, contractors, and, to the extent of their engagement, third-party service providers and Group personnel performing functions for the Company. It also addresses conflicts involving the Company’s shareholders and Group Entities. It is reviewed at least annually and on any material change to the Company’s activities, structure, or regulatory obligations, and is approved by the Board.

The Company operates as a principal Virtual Asset Broker-Dealer providing Spot and Over-the-Counter (OTC) dealing services. Because the Company deals as principal, acting as counterparty to client transactions, it recognises that its dealing model gives rise to an inherent conflict between the Company’s interests and those of its clients, and it manages that conflict as a central feature of this Policy.
REGULATORY BASIS AND RULEBOOK ALIGNMENT
This Policy gives effect to the conflict-of-interest and fair-treatment obligations applicable to a VASP conducting Broker-Dealer Services, and in particular to the following, without limitation:

VARA Market Conduct Rulebook, including the requirements to act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interests of clients, to treat clients fairly, to identify and manage conflicts of interest, to maintain Insider Lists and manage Inside Information, and the requirements governing Board and Staff positions, prior approvals, and disclosures;

VARA Company Rulebook, including the corporate governance, segregation of duties, Fit and Proper, Responsible Individual, related-party, and outsourcing requirements relevant to the avoidance and management of conflicts;

VARA Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook, including the compliance-management, risk-management, record-keeping, and anti-bribery and corruption requirements, and the treatment of conflicts as a market-conduct and compliance risk within the enterprise risk framework;

VARA Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook, including the best-execution, dealing-as-principal, order-handling, and disclosure requirements through which conflicts between the Company’s dealing interests and client orders are managed; and
the Regulations and Dubai Law No. (4) of 2022, including the market-offence provisions concerning insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of Inside Information, and market manipulation.

A summary mapping of the principal areas of this Policy to the relevant VARA Rulebooks is set out in the Rulebook Mapping table in Section 12. The mapping is indicative and does not limit the application of any Rulebook provision.
DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
In this Policy, capitalised terms have the meanings given in the VARA Rulebooks and the Regulations, unless otherwise defined. In particular:

“Conflict of Interest” means any situation in which the interests of the Company, a Group Entity, a member of the Board, a member of Senior Management, a Responsible Individual, a member of Staff, or a shareholder, conflict, or may conflict, with the duties owed to a client or with the interests of a client or the Company, or in which any such person is or may be influenced by a competing interest in a manner that could reasonably impair objectivity;

“Group” and “Group Entity” mean, respectively, the wider MetaComp group of which the Company forms part (ultimately owned by Metacomp Group (Cayman) Limited and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner) and any entity within that Group, including affiliated licensed entities;
“Responsible Individual” or “RI” has the meaning given in the VARA Company Rulebook;
“Inside Information” and “Insider List” have the meanings given in the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook;
“Staff” means the employees, officers, contractors, secondees, and temporary personnel of the Company; and
“Conflicts Register” means the conflicts of interest register maintained by the Compliance Function under Section 9.

References to a person having an “interest” include direct and indirect interests, financial and non-financial interests, and interests held by a Connected Person (including a family member or close associate).
GENERAL PRINCIPLES AND CONFIRMATIONS
The Company’s approach to conflicts of interest is founded on the following principles:
the interests of clients take precedence, and the Company acts honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interests of its clients;
the Company takes all reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest involving the Company, its Group, its Board, its Staff, its clients, and its investors;

where a conflict cannot reasonably be avoided, it is identified, assessed, managed, recorded in the Conflicts Register, and disclosed to affected clients in a clear, fair, and not misleading manner before the Company acts, so that the client can make an informed decision;

Disclosure is not relied upon as a substitute for the effective prevention, management or mitigation of a conflict. Where disclosure is required under the VARA Rulebooks, including where an interest may reasonably impair the objectivity of the Company, a member of the Board or any member of Staff, the Company promptly discloses the nature of the conflict to the affected client and, to the extent that the affected client’s interests can be sufficiently protected, manages and minimises the conflict through appropriate measures;

no member of the Board, Senior Management, or Staff participates in a decision, transaction, or relationship in which that person has a material interest without appropriate management, recusal, or approval; and

the Company does not hold itself out as independent in respect of any Virtual Asset Activity where a conflict or interest would render such a representation misleading, and it discloses its principal capacity and interests accordingly.

The Board confirms, and this Policy records, that reasonable efforts are taken to avoid conflicts of interest, and that conflicts which cannot be avoided are appropriately managed and disclosed in accordance with the VARA Rulebooks.
DECLARATION OF ACTUAL AND POTENTIAL CONFLICTS

The Company has assessed the actual and potential conflicts of interest that may arise across its business, having regard to its ownership structure, its Group relationships, its principal-dealing model, and the roles of its Board, Senior Management, Responsible Individuals, and Staff. The principal categories, and the Company’s declaration in respect of each, are set out below.
Company and client conflicts (principal dealing)

As a principal broker-dealer, the Company acts as counterparty to client transactions and earns a spread or margin on dealing. This gives rise to an inherent and continuing conflict between the Company’s interest in the pricing and profitability of a transaction and the client’s interest in obtaining the best possible result. The Company declares this conflict openly and manages it through the controls described in Section 7 and in its Broker-Dealer Operational Policy and Procedures, including transparent pre-disclosed pricing, best-execution and fair-treatment controls, and inventory-exposure limits monitored independently of the dealing function.
Shareholder, Board, and Senior Management conflicts

Conflicts may arise from the interests, roles, or relationships of the Company’s shareholders, Board members, Senior Management, and Responsible Individuals, including where an individual holds a concurrent role, directorship, shareholding, or economic interest within the Group or in an external entity, or where the Ultimate Beneficial Owner or a Director holds group-level positions. The Company declares that certain of its key individuals hold roles at Group level, and manages the resulting conflicts through the governance separation, recusal, and disclosure arrangements described in Sections 6 and 7. The specific declared interests of Board members and Senior Management are recorded in the Conflicts Register and in individual declarations maintained by the Compliance Function.
Staff conflicts

Conflicts may arise from the personal interests, outside activities, personal account dealing, gifts and hospitality, or relationships of Staff. Staff conflicts are managed through the Code of Conduct, personal-account-dealing controls, gifts-and-hospitality rules and registers, outside-business-interest approvals, and the declaration requirements in Section 8.
Related-party and intra-group (Group Entity) conflicts

The Company operates within a wider Group and benefits from Group infrastructure, governance experience, and technology capabilities under documented, arm’s-length intra-group service arrangements. Conflicts may arise from these relationships, including in relation to the shared-services model, the pricing of intra-group services, the use of Group-affiliated counterparties or infrastructure, and the alignment of incentives between the Company and Group Entities. The Company declares its material Group relationships, conducts related-party dealings at arm’s length under Service Level Agreements, and manages the resulting conflicts as described in Section 6.4.
Conflicts from external interests and multiple mandates

Conflicts may arise where a Board member, member of Senior Management, or member of Staff holds an external directorship, shareholding, advisory role, or other interest, or where competing client interests arise. Such interests are subject to prior approval and periodic disclosure under Section 8 and are recorded in the Conflicts Register.
GOVERNANCE, ROLES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES
The identification, management, and oversight of conflicts of interest are embedded in the Company’s governance structure and Three Lines of Defence model.
Board of Directors

The Board holds ultimate responsibility for the effective management of conflicts of interest. The Board approves this Policy, oversees the adequacy and effectiveness of the conflicts framework, considers and approves the management of material conflicts (including conflicts involving Board members, Senior Management, shareholders, and Group Entities), and ensures that a conflicted individual does not participate in the relevant decision. The Board’s consideration of material conflicts, and the outcomes, are recorded in the Board minutes and reflected in the Conflicts Register.
Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee (ARCC)

The ARCC supports the Board by reviewing the Conflicts Register, material conflicts and their management, related-party dealings, and the effectiveness of the conflicts framework, and escalates material matters to the Board. The ARCC is chaired by a Director who does not hold an executive management role.
Senior Management and Responsible Individuals

Senior Management implements this Policy, embeds a culture in which conflicts are proactively identified and disclosed, and ensures that business and operational functions apply the required controls. The Responsible Individuals are accountable to VARA for the conduct of licensed activities, including the fair treatment of clients and the management of conflicts within their areas of responsibility.
Compliance Function

The Compliance Function, headed by the Chief Compliance Officer and MLRO, is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the conflicts framework, including maintaining the Conflicts Register, receiving and assessing declarations, advising on the management of conflicts, monitoring adherence, overseeing related-party and personal-account-dealing controls, and reporting to the ARCC and the Board. The Compliance Function is independent of the revenue-generating dealing function and has direct access to the Board and the ARCC.
Related-party and intra-group dealings

Intra-group service arrangements are documented through Service Level Agreements entered into on an arm’s-length basis. The Company identifies all transactions with Related Parties and applies the requirements of Part II.G of the VARA Company Rulebook, in addition to the general conflict-management controls in this Policy.

Prior Board consent. The Company shall not enter into a transaction with any Related Party without the prior written consent of the Board where the value of the transaction exceeds five percent (5%) of the Company’s issued share capital. If there is a significant change to the terms of such transaction, further written consent of the Board shall be obtained before the Company enters into the transaction on the changed terms.
Voting restriction. A Related Party with an interest in a transaction requiring Board consent under paragraph (a) shall not participate in voting on the relevant Board decision.

Prior notice to VARA. Before entering into any transaction with a Related Party, the Board shall provide VARA with prior notice identifying the Related Party and providing details of the transaction, including the nature and benefit of the Related Party’s involvement, together with written confirmation that the transaction terms are fair, reasonable and proportional to the interests of the Company’s shareholders.

Access to records. The Company shall allow its clients and shareholders to review the Company records and documents relating to transactions with Related Parties in accordance with the Company Rulebook.

Related Party Transactions Register. The Compliance Function shall maintain a register of transactions with Related Parties recording the names of the relevant Related Parties, the relevant transactions, and the actions taken in relation to them in sufficient detail. The register may be maintained as a dedicated module of the Company’s compliance management system and shall be reconciled, where relevant, with entries in the Conflicts Register.

Regulatory reporting. The Company shall report all transactions with Related Parties to VARA monthly, and otherwise upon request by VARA, including the details of those transactions. The Company shall also provide any documents and other information relating to such transactions as reasonably requested by VARA.

General safeguards. Related-party and intra-group arrangements shall remain subject to independent Compliance review and shall not be entered into on terms that are detrimental to clients or that compromise the Company’s regulatory compliance or independence.
6. 6 Loans to Board, Senior Management, and Responsible Individuals

The Company shall notify VARA and obtain VARA approval before making any loan to a member of the Board, Senior Management, or a Responsible Individual. Any such notification shall include full details of the name of the proposed recipient, the amount of the loan, and the purpose of the loan. No such loan shall be advanced until the required VARA approval has been obtained.
IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND MITIGATION MEASURES

For each identified conflict, the Company assesses the nature of the conflict and the extent to which it may reasonably impair the objectivity of the Company or any individual in transactions or relationships with clients, and it assesses the impact of the conflict on the Company’s independence, on its clients, and on its regulatory compliance.
Assessment of nature and impact

The assessment considers, at a minimum: the nature and source of the conflict; the parties involved and their relationship to the Company or the Group; whether the conflict is actual, potential, or perceived; whether it may reasonably impair objectivity or the fair treatment of clients; the materiality of the interest; the impact on the Company’s independence (including any implication where the Company represents itself as independent in conducting Virtual Asset Activities); the impact on affected clients; and the impact on the Company’s compliance with the Regulations and the VARA Rulebooks. Each conflict is assigned a materiality rating that determines the management measures applied and the level of approval and disclosure required.
Mitigation and management measures
The Company applies one or more of the following measures, proportionate to the nature and materiality of the conflict:

disclosure to affected clients, in a clear, fair, and not misleading manner and in durable form, of the general nature and sources of the conflict and the steps taken to mitigate it, provided before the Company undertakes the relevant business, so that the client can make an informed decision;

fair-treatment and best-execution arrangements, including transparent pre-disclosed pricing and spreads, fair allocation, and the disclosure of the Company’s principal capacity and of fees or commission retained on a transaction;

restrictions on participation, including the recusal of a conflicted Director, manager, or member of Staff from any decision, deliberation, or vote in which that person has a material interest, and restrictions on that person influencing the relevant matter;

information barriers (including physical, systems, and access controls) to prevent the inappropriate flow of Inside Information or client information between functions, individuals, or Group Entities where a conflict so requires;
segregation of duties, including the separation of the dealing function from the independent risk monitoring of inventory exposure and from compliance oversight of best execution and fair treatment;

controls over personal account dealing, gifts and hospitality, outside business interests, and inducements, including the prohibition on paying or receiving any monetary or non-monetary benefit for routing client orders except necessary execution fees;
declining to act, or requiring divestment of the relevant interest or resignation from the relevant external role, where a conflict cannot otherwise be adequately managed; and
escalation to, and approval by, the ARCC or the Board of material conflicts and the means of managing them.

Where the organisational and administrative arrangements are not sufficient to ensure, with reasonable confidence, that the risk of damage to a client’s interests will be prevented, the Company clearly discloses the general nature and sources of the conflict, and the mitigating steps taken, to the client before undertaking business, and considers whether it is appropriate to proceed at all.
DECLARATION, PRIOR APPROVAL, AND PERIODIC DISCLOSURE OBLIGATIONS

Board members, Senior Management, Responsible Individuals, and Staff are required to identify and declare actual, potential, and perceived conflicts of interest promptly on appointment, on any change of circumstances, and in relation to any specific matter in which they have an interest, by submitting a declaration to the Compliance Function.

In accordance with the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook requirements governing Board and Staff positions, all Board members and Staff must obtain prior written approval from the Company before opening, modifying, or closing Virtual Asset positions, before increasing or decreasing shareholdings in other legal entities, and before taking up directorships in other entities. At least every six (6) months, all Board members and Staff must notify the Company of all Virtual Asset positions held directly or indirectly and all shareholdings and directorships in other entities. Records of all notifications and approvals are maintained within the compliance management system, and any conflict identified is managed under Section 7, including divestment or resignation where required.

Where the Company has any information or reason to believe that a Board member or member of Staff is likely to cause, or has caused, an actual or potential conflict of interest, the Company shall take all necessary actions to ensure that the conflict of interest is removed. Such actions may include requiring the relevant person to divest relevant Virtual Asset positions or shareholdings, to resign from the board of another legal entity, or to take any other action necessary to remove the conflict, whether in relation to the other entity or the Company.

Prior to the commencement of their appointment, engagement, or employment with the Company, the Company shall notify all Board members and Staff in writing of their obligations under Rule VI.B of the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook, including the applicable prior-approval, periodic-notification, and conflict-removal requirements. The Company shall retain evidence of such written notification and acknowledgement within the compliance management system.

The Company shall maintain complete and up-to-date Insider Lists of all Entities that have or may have access to Inside Information in the course of the Company’s business or in carrying out their respective roles for the Company, including members of the Board, Staff, Group Entities and relevant Group personnel, advisers, accountants, and other third-party agents and service providers, and shall update the Insider Lists while the relevant information remains Inside Information.
Each Insider List shall include, at a minimum:
(a) the identity of each Entity having access to Inside Information;
(b) the reason for including that Entity in the Insider List;
(c) the date and time at which that Entity obtained access to Inside Information; and
(d) the date on which the Insider List was drawn up.

The Company shall promptly update an Insider List where the reason for inclusion changes, a new Entity obtains access, or an Entity ceases to have access, and each update shall record the date of the update and the date and time when the change triggering the update occurred.

The Company shall retain each Insider List for at least eight (8) years after it is drawn up or updated and shall provide any Insider List to VARA upon request. The Company shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that every Entity included on an Insider List acknowledges in writing the legal and regulatory duties arising from access to Inside Information and is aware of the sanctions applicable to Insider Dealing and unlawful disclosure of Inside Information. The Compliance Function shall retain the written acknowledgements and monitor compliance with these requirements.
ONGOING MONITORING AND THE CONFLICTS OF INTEREST REGISTER

The Company maintains a Conflicts of Interest Register as the central record of identified conflicts and their management. The Register is maintained by the Compliance Function, reviewed by the ARCC, and made available to VARA on request.

For each conflict, the Register records, at a minimum: the nature and source of the conflict and whether it may reasonably impair objectivity; the names and positions of the parties involved and their relationship to the Company or the Group, including any Board member or member of Staff with a material interest; the impact assessment (including impact on independence, clients, and regulatory compliance); the mitigation measures applied (including disclosure, fair-treatment arrangements, restrictions on participation or voting, and information barriers); the decisions taken and any Board or ARCC consideration and outcome; the remedial actions and their status; and the date and owner of each entry.

The Company monitors conflicts on an ongoing basis, including through the declaration and periodic-disclosure process (Section 8), compliance monitoring and testing, review of related-party dealings, personal-account-dealing surveillance, and trade surveillance of best execution and fair treatment. Material conflicts, and the effectiveness of the conflicts framework, are reported to the ARCC and the Board, and the Board’s consideration and outcomes are documented. Records relating to conflicts are retained for a minimum of eight (8) years in accordance with the VARA record-keeping requirements.
The standing contents of the Conflicts Register are summarised below.
Field
Content recorded
Reference / date
Unique reference and date of identification and last update.
Nature of conflict
Description and source; actual, potential, or perceived; whether it may reasonably impair objectivity.
Parties involved
Names and positions; relationship to the Company or Group; material interest held.
Impact assessment
Impact on independence, clients, and regulatory compliance; materiality rating.
Mitigation measures
Disclosure, fair-treatment arrangements, restrictions on participation or voting, information barriers, segregation, divestment or recusal.
Decisions and Board consideration
Decisions taken; ARCC or Board consideration and outcome where relevant.
Remedial actions and status
Actions required, owner, target date, and status.
DISCLOSURE TO CLIENTS AND REPRESENTATIONS OF INDEPENDENCE

The Company discloses to clients, in its Client Agreements, Risk Disclosure Statement, and pre-trade and trade-confirmation disclosures, that it acts as principal counterparty to their transactions, together with its spreads, fees, and the basis of its pricing, so that clients understand the Company’s interest in their transactions.

In addition, in accordance with Rule I.B.1(a) of the VARA Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook, the Company shall publish on its website in a prominent place, or make available by other publicly accessible means, a detailed description of any actual or potential conflicts of interest arising out of its Broker-Dealer activities and how those conflicts are managed. The Compliance Function shall ensure that this public disclosure remains accurate and is updated whenever there is a material change to the Company’s activities or conflict profile.

Where disclosure is required under the applicable VARA Rulebooks, including where an interest may reasonably impair objectivity, the Company promptly discloses to the affected client, in a clear, fair and not misleading manner, the nature and sources of the conflict and the measures taken to manage or minimise it. Where organisational or administrative arrangements are not sufficient to ensure, with reasonable confidence, that the risk of damage to a client’s interests will be prevented, such disclosure shall be made before the Company undertakes the relevant business and the Company shall also consider whether it is appropriate to proceed at all. The Company does not represent itself as independent in conducting any Virtual Asset Activity where an interest or conflict would render such a representation misleading. Where the Company or a Group Entity has a material interest in a transaction or relationship, that interest is disclosed and the representation of independence is qualified accordingly.
TOKEN ISSUANCE CONFLICTS (NOT APPLICABLE)

The Company does not undertake Virtual Asset issuance and does not conduct token sales on its own account. Accordingly, the issuance-specific conflict-of-interest requirements, including controls addressing insider access to issuance terms, influence over allocation, secondary-market trading strategies, and conflicts arising from overlapping roles in governance and token economics, are not applicable to the Company’s current licensed scope.

Should the Company undertake VA issuance, or Placement and Distribution of Virtual Assets on behalf of third-party Issuers, in future, it would first obtain any required VARA authorisation and extend this Policy to incorporate the issuance-specific conflict controls before commencing such activity. Those controls would address, at a minimum: restrictions on related parties and insiders participating in or influencing token sales or receiving preferential allocations; management of insider access to issuance terms and pricing; controls over allocation decisions; controls over secondary-market trading and market-making strategies in an issued asset; information barriers between issuance, dealing, and advisory functions; and the management of conflicts arising from any overlapping roles in the governance of an Issuer and in the economics of an issued token.
VARA RULEBOOK MAPPING

REVIEW, APPROVAL, AND CERTIFICATION

This Policy is approved by the Board of Directors of Metacomp FZE and is reviewed at least annually, or earlier upon any material change to the Company’s activities, structure, governance, or regulatory obligations. The Board confirms that the Company takes all reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest involving the Company, its Group, its Board, its Staff, its clients, and its investors; that conflicts which cannot be avoided are appropriately managed, recorded in the Conflicts Register, and disclosed to affected clients; that a conflicted individual does not participate in the relevant decision; and that the Company undertakes to maintain this framework in compliance with the VARA Market Conduct, Company, and Compliance and Risk Management Rulebooks.

best-execution.title: Best Execution Policy
best-execution.subtitle: Best Execution Policy and Procedures — Metacomp Virtual Assets Broker & Dealer Services FZE. Broker-Dealer Services | Spot and OTC principal dealing.

blocks.text: 1. Purpose, Scope and Status

This Best Execution Policy and Procedures (the “Policy”) establishes the framework by which Metacomp Virtual Assets Broker & Dealer Services FZE (“Metacomp FZE” or the “Company”) will exercise reasonable diligence when executing client orders in Virtual Assets so as to obtain the best possible result for the client under prevailing market conditions.

The Policy applies to all Spot and OTC Broker-Dealer Services undertaken by the Company at launch, including RFQ transactions, principal execution against Company inventory and riskless-principal/back-to-back execution using approved Liquidity Providers (“LPs”). It applies to Retail, Qualified and Institutional Investors and to all Staff involved in pricing, quoting, execution, liquidity sourcing, settlement, supervision, Compliance and Risk oversight.

The Company is pre-operational. Where a final LP, quantitative threshold, technology configuration or production control is not yet confirmed, this Policy states the control standard to be implemented and evidenced before go-live rather than assuming that the control is already operational.
2. Regulatory Basis

This Policy is designed to implement Part II.A (Best Execution) and Part II.B (Dealing as Principal) of the VARA Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook, read together with the VARA Market Conduct Rulebook, Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook, Company Rulebook, Technology and Information Rulebook, the Virtual Assets and Related Activities Regulations 2023, and applicable VARA Rules, Directives and licence conditions, as amended from time to time.

The Company shall exercise reasonable diligence to obtain the most favourable price for each client order under prevailing market conditions while also giving due consideration to costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size, nature and any other relevant execution consideration. Responsibility for Best Execution remains with Metacomp FZE and shall not be delegated to an LP, Group Entity, technology provider or other third party.
3. Definitions
Term
Meaning
Best Execution
The obligation to take reasonable steps and exercise reasonable diligence to obtain the best possible result for the client, having regard to the applicable execution factors.
Principal
Metacomp FZE acts as the client’s direct counterparty.
Riskless Principal
After receiving a client order, Metacomp FZE enters into a matching or substantially matching offsetting transaction with an approved LP at or about the same time.
RFQ
Request for Quote: a client requests an executable principal quote which the client may accept or decline within its validity period.
Inventory
The Company’s own Virtual Asset or fiat holdings used for operational liquidity and permitted principal dealing.
Liquidity Provider
An approved third-party counterparty used to source pricing or offset client transactions.
Execution Venue / Market
A market, VASP, LP or other permissible source of executable liquidity considered for an order.
4. Execution Model and Application of Best Execution

At Phase 1, Metacomp FZE operates a principal-only Spot and OTC model. It does not operate an exchange, multilateral order book or client-to-client matching facility and does not act as agent for client orders. A client transaction may be satisfied (i) against the Company’s own inventory, or (ii) through a contemporaneous or near-contemporaneous back-to-back offset with an approved LP.

Because Phase 1 client orders are satisfied by the Company dealing as principal, the Company shall apply the Best Execution standard to those orders. The limited exceptions in Rule II.A.2 of the Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook are not relied upon for the Company’s principal-only Phase 1 model. Any future change to the execution model must be assessed by Compliance and approved through the Company’s governance and regulatory change process before implementation.

When dealing as principal, the Company shall not use or otherwise deal in Client Money or Client VAs except as expressly permitted under applicable VARA requirements and the Company’s Client Asset Safeguarding, Segregation and Reconciliation Policy.
5. Best Execution Factors

The Company shall consider all relevant circumstances of an order. Price is expected to be a primary factor for ordinary Spot and OTC execution, but it is not considered in isolation where another factor materially affects the overall result for the client.
Factor
Application
Price
Executable market/reference price available for the relevant VA and transaction direction, adjusted only through the approved pricing methodology.
Costs
Explicit and implicit costs, including spread, fees, settlement/network costs and third-party execution costs where relevant.
Speed

Likelihood of execution
Depth and certainty available from inventory and/or LPs for the requested size.
Likelihood of settlement
Counterparty, banking, custody, blockchain and operational considerations affecting successful settlement.
Size and nature
Order size relative to available liquidity, market depth, block/OTC characteristics and potential market impact.
Market characteristics
Price, spreads, volatility, relative liquidity, market fragmentation and prevailing market conditions.
Liquidity sources checked
Number and quality of reasonably accessible Markets/LPs and availability of executable quotes.
Client terms/instructions
Any lawful and specific terms communicated by the client, including time sensitivity and settlement requirements.
6. Pricing and Quote Construction

The dealing function shall use an approved and documented pricing methodology. Quotes must be based on observable and reasonably current market information and/or executable LP prices, subject to controls appropriate to the relevant VA, order size and prevailing market conditions.
Reference prices and LP quotes must be obtained from approved sources and time-stamped where technically feasible.
Any spread or mark-up applied by the Company must be determined under an approved methodology, consistently applied and disclosed to clients in accordance with the Client Agreement and Fee Schedule.
The Company shall not widen a spread selectively because of non-public client information, anticipated client urgency or another conflict of interest.
Stale, erroneous or clearly anomalous prices must not be used without documented review and approval under the exception process.
For large or illiquid OTC transactions, the dealing function shall document the liquidity checks and rationale supporting the final executable quote.
7. Liquidity Provider and Market Selection

LPs and other execution counterparties shall be subject to onboarding, due diligence and approval before use. The approved list, final legal entities and jurisdictions are to be completed before go-live.
Regulatory status, reputation and financial standing;
quality, competitiveness and reliability of pricing;
depth and capacity across supported VAs and transaction sizes;
execution and settlement performance;
technology/API resilience and operational support;
counterparty, concentration, sanctions and jurisdiction risk;
conflicts, inducements or commercial arrangements that could bias routing; and
ability to provide records needed for Metacomp FZE to evidence Best Execution.
No LP may be selected solely because it provides higher commercial benefit to the Company where doing so would result in a worse execution outcome for the client.
8. Order and RFQ Handling Procedures

All client orders/RFQs shall be captured through approved channels and recorded with sufficient information to reconstruct the transaction lifecycle. Orders must be handled promptly, fairly and in accordance with their terms.
Confirm client eligibility, KYC status and applicable restrictions before execution.
Validate available balance/funding and supported VA status.
Record the time of RFQ/order receipt and material client instructions.
Obtain relevant market/LP pricing and apply the approved quote methodology.
Present an executable quote with a defined validity period where applicable.
Record client acceptance/rejection and execution timestamp.
Where an LP offset is required, execute the hedge/back-to-back transaction under approved controls.
Generate the trade confirmation and complete settlement/reconciliation controls.
Retain quote inputs, execution records and exception evidence for regulatory review.
9. Specific Client Instructions

Where a client gives an unsolicited and lawful specific instruction that constrains execution, the Company shall follow the instruction promptly to the extent it is compatible with the Company’s principal-dealing model, licence and controls. The Company shall inform the client, where appropriate, that a specific instruction may prevent the Company from applying aspects of its ordinary Best Execution process to the element covered by that instruction.

The Company’s Phase 1 model does not permit a client to direct Metacomp FZE to act as agent or to route an order to a named venue in a manner inconsistent with the approved principal model. Such requests shall be declined or escalated.
10. Off-Market and OTC Execution

Where an order is executed off-Market, including through bilateral OTC execution or an offsetting transaction with an LP, Metacomp FZE retains the burden of demonstrating compliance with Best Execution. The dealing function shall therefore preserve sufficient contemporaneous evidence of market conditions, price sources, quotes checked, size/liquidity considerations and the rationale for the final client price.
11. Principal and Inventory Execution

Principal dealing is permitted only for satisfying client orders, permitted placement activity (if authorised in future) and management of Company inventory in accordance with the Broker-Dealer Services Rulebook and approved risk limits. The Company shall not undertake speculative proprietary trading as part of the Phase 1 business model.
Inventory execution must be priced against objective market information rather than an arbitrary internal price.
The fact that execution against inventory may be more profitable to the Company must not determine the client outcome.
Inventory and concentration limits shall be Board-approved and monitored by Risk.
Dealing Staff must not front-run, misuse client order information or delay execution to benefit the Company’s inventory position.
12. Conflicts of Interest

The Company shall identify and manage conflicts between competing client interests and between client orders and the Company’s own interests. Controls include functional segregation, approved pricing methodology, LP governance, prohibition of payment-for-order-flow arrangements that impair client outcomes, surveillance, escalation to Compliance and maintenance of conflicts records.
Where a conflict cannot be effectively prevented or managed so that the client is protected, the Company shall decline or suspend the transaction as appropriate.
13. Exceptional Market Conditions and Price Formation

During high volatility, illiquidity, market fragmentation, technology disruption or absence of reliable pricing information, the Company remains responsible for taking reasonable steps to seek Best Execution. The Company shall not treat the unavailability of one or more liquidity sources as removing that obligation.
check alternative approved pricing/liquidity sources where reasonably available;
increase manual review or require senior dealing approval for abnormal spreads or large deviations;
document valuation drivers and rationale where conventional pricing is unavailable;
apply quote-size limits, shorter quote-validity periods or temporary execution restrictions where necessary to protect clients and market integrity; and
escalate material execution disruption to Compliance, Risk and Senior Management.
14. Execution Quality Monitoring

Compliance and the dealing function shall maintain a documented monitoring programme proportionate to the business. Where Metacomp FZE internalises client order flow and/or routes/offsets flow with other entities, execution quality shall be reviewed at least quarterly, including comparison against alternative reasonably available Markets or liquidity sources.
Monitoring Area
Illustrative Measure / KRI
Price quality
Client execution price versus contemporaneous benchmark/reference price; unexplained slippage.
Spread quality
Actual spread/mark-up versus approved parameters and comparable market conditions.
LP competitiveness
Quote win rate, price dispersion and quality by LP and VA.
Execution performance
Reject/failure rate, latency, re-quotes and exception frequency.
Settlement quality
Settlement failures, delays and reconciliation breaks attributable to execution counterparties.
Concentration
Share of offset volume by LP / top LP concentration.
Complaints
Best Execution, pricing or execution-related complaints and root causes.

Proposed quantitative thresholds shall be calibrated using pre-go-live testing and early operating data and approved through the Company’s risk and governance framework. They shall not be presented as VARA-prescribed thresholds unless VARA expressly prescribes them.
15. Execution Exceptions and Escalation

An execution exception includes a material deviation from approved pricing methodology, use of an unapproved LP/source, stale or erroneous price, execution outside approved limits, system failure, significant settlement risk, suspected conflict, or inability to evidence the execution rationale.
The dealing function shall stop or restrict execution where continuing could cause unfair client outcomes or regulatory breach.
Material exceptions shall be escalated promptly to Compliance and Risk and, where appropriate, Senior Management.
The reason, decision, client impact, remediation and any compensation decision shall be documented.
Compliance shall assess whether the matter constitutes a reportable breach, market conduct issue or other notification obligation to VARA.
16. Systems, Capacity and Resilience

The Company shall maintain systems with sufficient capacity and capability to receive, price, execute, record and settle client orders through approved channels. Pre-go-live testing shall cover pricing feeds, RFQ/order capture, time stamping, LP connectivity, execution controls, audit trails, failover and exception handling. Material technology incidents affecting execution shall be handled under the Technology, Incident Management and BCDR frameworks.
17. Client Disclosure and Notification

Before providing Broker-Dealer Services, clients shall receive clear information on Metacomp FZE’s principal capacity, execution methodology, relevant fees/spreads, material conflicts and the operation of this Policy through the Client Agreement and related disclosures. The Company shall notify clients with whom it has an ongoing relationship of material changes to its order execution arrangements or this Policy, in accordance with applicable VARA requirements and contractual notice provisions.
18. Records and Evidence

The Company shall maintain records sufficient to demonstrate compliance with this Policy and reconstruct each transaction. Records shall include client instructions, RFQs/orders, quote inputs, reference prices, LP quotes, timestamps, execution/offset details, trade confirmations, settlement records, exceptions, approvals, monitoring outputs and client communications. Records shall be retained for the period required by applicable VARA requirements and made available to VARA on request.
19. Governance and Responsibilities
Role
Responsibilities
Board of Directors
Approve the Policy and material changes; oversee the execution framework, material conflicts and risk limits.
Senior Management
Implement the Policy, ensure adequate resources/systems and remediate material deficiencies.
Head of Dealing / Dealing Function
Apply pricing and execution methodology; evidence liquidity checks; manage inventory/LP execution within limits; escalate exceptions.
Compliance Officer
Independent monitoring, conflicts oversight, exception review, regulatory interpretation, breach assessment and reporting.
Risk Function
Monitor inventory, counterparty, liquidity and concentration risks and relevant KRIs.
Operations / Finance
Settlement, reconciliations, break management and supporting evidence.
Technology
Maintain execution-system availability, access controls, logging, change management and resilience.
20. Training

Relevant Staff shall receive training before performing execution-related responsibilities and periodically thereafter. Training shall cover Best Execution, principal dealing, pricing, conflicts, market abuse/front-running, recordkeeping, exception escalation and the use of execution systems.
21. Review, Testing and Change Management

The effectiveness of this Policy and its controls shall be assessed and reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to the business model, client categories, supported VAs, pricing methodology, execution channel, LP arrangements, technology, applicable law or VARA requirements. Deficiencies shall be documented, assigned, remediated and tracked to closure.

Any material change to order execution arrangements shall undergo Compliance and Risk review, appropriate governance approval, client notification where required, and regulatory assessment before implementation.

Documented methodology and governance for mark-ups/spreads by product/order type.

Production configuration, permissions, maker-checker controls and audit trail.

Annexure A. Execution Decision Framework
For each client order/RFQ, the dealing function should be able to evidence the following decision sequence:

2. Identify relevant market conditions and approved pricing sources.
3. Determine available inventory and/or approved LP liquidity.
